question: In Harry Potter, the prophecy about the one who could defeat Voldemort fitted two baby boys born at the end of July. Harry was one. Which Hogwarts classmate was the other?
source_excerpt: Neville's birthday falls on July 30, while Harry's falls on July 31.

extra.why_interesting: Players assume Harry was always destined to be the Chosen One. In fact the prophecy fitted two boys, and Voldemort's own choice of which one to attack is what made Harry the hero.

topicality.rationale: Book plot trivia from Harry Potter; general culture with no news hook.

extra.verification_notes: Dumbledore states in Order of the Phoenix that the prophecy could have meant Harry or Neville, born 31 and 30 July 1980; see https://www.harrypotter.com/features/eerie-similarities-between-harry-potter-and-neville-longbottom

explanation: Neville was born on 30 July, one day before Harry, and his parents had also defied Voldemort three times. Voldemort chose to attack the Potters, and that choice is what marked Harry as his equal.

question: Severus Snape's Patronus takes exactly the same form as Lily Potter's. What animal is it?
source_excerpt: Snape's Patronus was a doe... the same as my mother's, because he loved her for nearly all of his life

extra.why_interesting: Players know Harry's stag but rarely link it to its emotional mirror. The answer unlocks the whole Snape twist: his Patronus matches the woman he loved, and it pairs with James's stag.

topicality.rationale: Harry Potter book lore; long-established fiction, not tied to current news.

extra.verification_notes: Canon (Deathly Hallows) states Snape's Patronus was a doe, the same as Lily's; no contradicting or newer information found (https://www.hp-lexicon.org/?p=270).

explanation: When Dumbledore sees it he asks, 'After all this time?' and Snape answers, 'Always.' It also pairs with James Potter's stag, which is why Harry's own Patronus is a stag.

question: Hagrid owns a giant three-headed dog that guards a trapdoor at Hogwarts in the first Harry Potter story. He gave this fearsome beast a very cuddly name. What is it?
source_excerpt: Fluffy was a male three-headed dog that Hagrid cared for and lent to Dumbledore to guard the Philosopher's Stone.

extra.why_interesting: A monstrous three-headed guard dog sounds like it should have a terrifying name. The joke is that Hagrid gave it the softest pet name imaginable.

topicality.rationale: Fixed literary trivia from a 1997 book; no news angle.

extra.verification_notes: Fluffy is Hagrid's three-headed dog guarding the trapdoor in Philosopher's Stone, per https://harrypotter.fandom.com/wiki/Fluffy; no newer event changes this.

explanation: Only Hagrid would call a three-headed monster Fluffy. The weakness the trio discovers is that a little music sends all three heads to sleep.

question: When Harry asks Dumbledore what he sees in the Mirror of Erised, Dumbledore names a modest piece of clothing he wishes people would give him for Christmas. What does he claim to see himself holding?
source_excerpt: I see myself holding a pair of thick, woollen socks.

extra.why_interesting: The mirror shows your deepest desire, so you'd expect the greatest wizard alive to see something grand. Instead he names a humble household item, which is a joke that also hides a sadder truth.

topicality.rationale: Book-content trivia with no current-news hook.

extra.verification_notes: Dumbledore says in Philosopher's Stone that he sees himself holding a pair of thick, woollen socks; nothing later contradicts this (https://www.harrypotter.com/features/what-we-learned-about-professor-dumbledore-from-the-mirror-of-erised).

explanation: He grumbles that he never gets socks because people insist on giving him books. Many readers later suspected he wasn't telling Harry the whole truth.

question: Dumbledore's full name is a long chain of grand-sounding names, but one of his middle names is strikingly ordinary. It is the same as the hero of a famous Monty Python film. What is that name?

extra.why_interesting: Players expect a string of grand, old-fashioned wizard names. One of them is a completely everyday modern name, and the Monty Python clue gives a fair route to it.

topicality.rationale: Literary/film cross-reference trivia; timeless general culture.

extra.verification_notes: Dumbledore's full name is Albus Percival Wulfric Brian Dumbledore, and Brian is the hero of Monty Python's Life of Brian (per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albus_Dumbledore).

explanation: His full name is Albus Percival Wulfric Brian Dumbledore. 'Brian' tucked among all that grandeur is pure Rowling mischief.

question: The Hogwarts school motto sounds grand in Latin, but in plain English it is simply a warning never to tickle a certain sleeping creature. Which creature?
source_excerpt: Draco dormiens nunquam titillandus: Latin for 'Never tickle a sleeping dragon', the motto of Hogwarts.

extra.why_interesting: Players expect a grand Latin school motto about wisdom or honour. Instead it is practical, comic advice about not poking a dangerous beast.

topicality.rationale: Harry Potter book trivia about the school motto; general culture, not news.

extra.verification_notes: The Hogwarts motto 'Draco dormiens nunquam titillandus' means 'never tickle a sleeping dragon', so the answer Dragon is correct (https://www.hp-lexicon.org/thing/draco-dormiens-nunquam-titillandus/).

explanation: The motto is 'Draco dormiens nunquam titillandus', or 'Never tickle a sleeping dragon'. It is probably the most sensible school motto ever written.

question: Hermione's Patronus is an otter. Ron Weasley's Patronus is a small, scrappy breed of dog. Which breed?
source_excerpt: Ron’s Patronus is a Jack Russell Terrier.

extra.why_interesting: Hermione's otter is widely known, but Ron's scrappy little dog is a deeper cut. It also fits his character well, and an otter and a terrier make a fitting pair.

topicality.rationale: Book/film lore detail about Ron's Patronus; timeless fandom trivia.

extra.verification_notes: Ron's Patronus is a Jack Russell terrier per the official Harry Potter site (https://www.harrypotter.com/features/web-7-times-rons-personality-matched-his-patronus); Hermione's otter is also correct.

explanation: Ron's Patronus is a Jack Russell terrier, and fans love that terriers are known for chasing otters. It is a hint at the couple long before they got together.

question: The Knight Bus, which picks up stranded witches and wizards, is a triple-decker that hurtles through Britain. What colour is it?
source_excerpt: purple and triple-decker with seats during the day and beds at night

extra.why_interesting: Players may assume it is a classic red London double-decker. It is in fact a violently purple triple-decker.

topicality.rationale: Fictional detail about the Knight Bus; general culture.

extra.verification_notes: The official Harry Potter site describes the Knight Bus as a purple triple-decker, which matches the question and the claimed answer.

explanation: It is a bright purple, three-storey bus that squeezes between traffic and lampposts. Its seats are brass beds instead of ordinary seats.

question: In Harry's third year, someone anonymously sends him a Firebolt, the fastest broom in the world. Hermione fears it came from a dangerous killer, and she is right about who sent it. Who was it?
source_excerpt: Sirius wrote that he was the one who sent the Firebolt, and that Crookshanks carried the order to the Owl Office for him.

extra.why_interesting: Hermione feared the broom came from a murderer trying to kill Harry. She was right about the sender and completely wrong about his motive.

topicality.rationale: Plot detail from Prisoner of Azkaban; timeless book trivia.

extra.verification_notes: In the book, Sirius Black sent the Firebolt anonymously and Hermione's suspicion was correct; I found no newer development that changes this, but I did not open a primary source for the exact passage (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sirius_Black).

explanation: It was his godfather, Sirius, who ordered it by owl using money from Harry's own Gringotts vault. He was trying to make up for twelve missed birthdays.
